events.description: 42. ORDER by Magistrate Judge Susan Prose on 2/18/2025. This court notes sua sponte that all Defendants move to dismiss this case asserting, among other things, that the court lacks subject matter jurisdiction for several reasons, including Eleventh Amendment immunity as to the State Defendants. Pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(b)(2), this court finds good cause to delay issuing the scheduling order until after the motions are resolved. The court also finds good cause to VACATE the telephonic status conference set for 3/5/2025. "Questions of jurisdiction should be resolved at the earliest stages of litigation, so as to conserve the time and resources of the [c]ourt and the parties. Thus, a stay of discovery during the pendency of a dispositive motion asserting a jurisdictional challenge may be appropriate and efficient." Am. Tradition Inst. v. Colorado, No. 11-cv-00859-WJM-KLM, 2011 WL 3705108, at *2 (D. Colo. Aug. 23, 2011). In particular, "Eleventh Amendment immunity entitles a state not only to protection from liability, but also from suit, including the burden of discovery, as a party, within the suit." Id. This court finds it appropriate and efficient in this case to not set a schedule until after the motions to dismiss are resolved. Accordingly, if the motions to dismiss are denied at least in part, the parties shall email prose_chambers@cod.uscourts.gov within three business days to set the scheduling conference. Objections to this order are due within fourteen days. Fed. R. Civ. P. 72(a). Failure to timely object waives the right to appeal from this ruling. Text Only Entry (sbplc1) (Entered: 02/18/2025)
